moveDecisions.rationale: The move establishes the central voluntary-separation account but does not by itself complete the motion-level justification of the alternatives.
The proportionality objection directly advances a central critical bridge while expressly addressing the qualified, self-chosen account rather than a crude torture model.
The move answers both duration and self-choice components, supports the finite-outcome bridge, and fairly acknowledges the force of the honest-error concern.
The move directly contacts both free separation and informed culpability, while its consequence most precisely supports the central involuntary-rejection bridge.
The move addresses both involuntary conviction and morally relevant influence, with stable core terminology though its scope and qualification remain partly implicit.
The candidate preserves the complete diagnostic contact with both motivated-reasoning agency and the proposed distinction between misinformation and culpable rejection.
The response explicitly contacts awareness and correction, sincere mistaken conviction, and the excusing role of misleading information across the live objections.
The move fully answers the free-refusal and adequate-information claims, centrally supports involuntary rejection, and advances a calibrated plausibility claim.
The death-cutoff challenge is a major route-level move, directly tests whether fair correction actually remains available, and presents that qualified challenge coherently and fairly.
This subsidiary move partially answers ongoing-consequence concerns but not hiddenness; its proposition is recoverable and its modal presentation is appropriately possibility-level.
The move contacts endless suffering and postmortem exit, but its claimed logical necessity overstates a speculative dissolution mechanism and leaves material scope unsettled.
The dilemma explicitly tests painful resistance, effective ability to exit, and informed free preference, thereby strongly advancing the central escape-dilemma bridge.
The reply answers the incapacity branch but not misinformation, attacks the central dilemma, and states a clear yet insufficiently qualified certainty about requesting grace.
The diagnostic contacts all three claims and represents them strongly, but its universalizing inference remains a subsidiary pressure with material warrant and calibration gaps.
The move fully and clearly tests whether an internally generated consequence can be substitutionally borne, while the asserted necessity remains somewhat stronger than its warrant.
The reply directly reframes the relevant consequence as death and exile and treats the objection fairly, but its categorical equivalence remains materially underwarranted.
The diagnostic question directly contacts the distinctiveness of death and the proposed spiritual dissolution, though it probes rather than decisively resolves those claims.
The move squarely tests whether crucifixion and forsakenness adequately match cumulative liability, with explicit contact at the decisive proportionality issue.
The reply fully contacts proportionality and relevant separation, represents the live objection adequately, and uses probabilistic language despite materially overstating its warrant.
